requirement: In Markdown, escaped roles and role-looking text in inline code, fenced code, or raw HTML MUST remain literal and MUST NOT count as references. Raw HTML means an HTML block, an HTML comment, or an inline HTML tag including its attributes; text between inline tags is ordinary Markdown. A `{req}` directive inside a fenced code example and a legacy inline `{req}` role MUST NOT define a requirement.
rationale:
I found no gaps. Every obligation has marked implementing code and a test that checks its outcome.

**Obligations and their code**
- **Escaped roles stay literal.** `is_escaped` in `src/lib.rs` counts the backslashes before the role, and `reference_roles` skips an escaped role. `is_escaped` also applies to non-Markdown input, but the text does not forbid that.
- **Inline code, fenced code and raw HTML stay literal.**
  - `protected_ranges` (`src/lib.rs`) collects ranges for `Tag::CodeBlock`, `Event::Code`, `Event::Html` (HTML blocks) and `Event::InlineHtml` (comments and tags, attributes included).
  - Text between inline tags is not in any range, so it stays ordinary Markdown.
  - `reference_roles` uses `is_protected`, and `markdown_fences` in `src/fenced.rs` uses `overlaps_protected`. Both skip protected text.
  - `is_markdown_path` in `src/outline/profile.rs` selects the Markdown profile for all Markdown extensions. `direct_references` in `src/terms.rs` applies the same rules to terms.
- **A `{req}` directive in a fenced code example does not define a requirement.** `definition_blocks` calls `code_block_ranges` and skips colon fences that overlap a code block.
- **A legacy inline `{req}` role does not define a requirement.** `definition_blocks` only recognizes colon fences, and `reference_roles` has no `{req}` role.

**Tests**
- `markdown_examples_and_escaped_references_stay_literal` (`src/lib.rs`) covers inline code, fenced code, an escaped role and double-backslash escapes.
- `roles_in_raw_html_stay_literal` (`src/lib.rs`) covers an HTML block, an HTML comment, an inline-tag attribute and text between inline tags, which stays a reference. It also checks that the same text in non-Markdown input is not protected.
- `code_examples_and_legacy_roles_remain_literal` and `colon_directives_render_markdown_bodies_and_legacy_roles_stay_literal` (`src/lib.rs`) cover a `{req}` directive in a code fence and a legacy `{req}` role.
- `every_markdown_extension_keeps_escaped_and_code_roles_literal` (`src/evidence.rs`) covers the `.md`, `.markdown`, `.MD` and `.Markdown` extensions. It also covers an escaped role, inline code, fenced code (including a `:::{cite}` fence), and an HTML attribute, with `.txt` as the non-Markdown control.
- `source_references_are_covered_by_evidence_inputs` (`src/evidence.rs`) covers the same literal cases when evidence inputs are validated.
- `references_in_requirement_bodies_are_scanned_as_markdown` (`src/lib.rs`) covers code fences inside requirement bodies.
- `term_dependencies_of_every_markdown_extension_skip_literal_roles` (`src/terms.rs`) covers term references.
- `markdown_fences_close_with_enough_colons_and_skip_code` (`src/fenced.rs`) covers a colon fence inside a code fence. It is not marked as a test of this requirement, but the other tests above already cover the same behavior.

A colon fence inside raw HTML has no direct test. It uses the same `protected_ranges` as the tested inline HTML cases, with no separate branch, so I did not count it as a gap.
